scope: Jurisdiction-neutral CBDC architecture research; public sources only
interpretation: Source facts are separated from proposed engineering decisions. Source status is not an assertion of legal force in an unspecified jurisdiction.

sources.title: Central bank digital currencies: foundational principles and core features
sources.publisher: Seven central banks and Bank for International Settlements
sources.status: Published joint analytical report; no issuance decision or binding law

claims.text: A CBDC represents a central-bank liability in the existing national unit of account.
The report prioritises monetary and financial stability, coexistence with existing money, and innovation; par conversion supports currency singleness.

sources.limits: General-purpose CBDC principles from participating authorities, not universal legal requirements or approval to issue.
sources.access: Official landing page read; indexed official PDF excerpts inspected. Direct full-PDF retrieval failed.

sources.title: Central bank digital currencies: system design and interoperability
sources.publisher: Seven central banks and Bank for International Settlements

claims.text: Issuance and redemption remain central-bank functions; ecosystem responsibilities include a rulebook, core infrastructure, processing and user-facing services.
The participating banks envisage public-private collaboration; account/token terminology is ambiguous across disciplines.

sources.limits: Describes design options and participants' preferences; does not require a particular ledger or exclude direct models in other jurisdictions.

sources.title: Central bank digital currencies: financial stability implications
sources.publisher: Seven central banks and Bank for International Settlements

claims.text: Holding and transaction limits and remuneration are alternative safeguards with adoption and financial-stability trade-offs.
A waterfall can route excess holdings to another account; safeguards can require additional data and processing.

sources.limits: Options are not calibrated rules for an unspecified country. PDF search metadata mislabels its title; the document cover confirms this title.
sources.access: Official PDF cover and safeguard sections read.

sources.title: Central bank digital currencies: System design
sources.publisher: Seven central banks and Bank for International Settlements
sources.status: Published joint analytical report; open design questions remain

claims.text: A two-tier design can combine centralised and decentralised components; privacy requires institutional, operational and technical choices.
Privacy technologies have performance and implementation trade-offs; offline settlement and quantum-era cryptography introduce additional risks.

sources.limits: Two-tier retail focus. Offline functionality is not endorsed as desirable for every jurisdiction. Experiments do not establish production readiness.

sources.title: Principles for financial market infrastructures
sources.status: Final international standards; domestic applicability requires assessment

claims.text: PFMI addresses legal basis, governance, risk management, settlement finality, operational risk and links.
Rules should identify when settlement is final. Central-bank-operated systems may tailor governance application to their mandates.

sources.limits: Applies to defined FMIs, including systemically important payment systems. This repository cannot self-certify PFMI compliance or assume every principle applies unchanged.
sources.access: Official final publication page and PDF relevant sections read.

sources.title: Guidance on cyber resilience for financial market infrastructures

claims.text: Resumption planning must preserve integrity and coordinate with affected participants.
The guidance addresses safe two-hour resumption capability and day-end settlement, while requiring contingency planning and judgment where resumption would increase risk.

sources.limits: An FMI benchmark, not a proven CBDC service-level agreement; it does not justify unsafe restart or replace a system-specific recovery design.
sources.access: Official final publication page and PDF relevant sections read.

sources.title: FAQs on the digital euro
sources.status: Living official project FAQ; prospective design and legislation-dependent issuance

claims.text: The proposed digital euro uses the same euro unit, with centralised settlement; its issuance decision follows adoption of its legislative framework.
The ECB distinguishes conditional payments from money restricted by purpose, time, place or counterparty; proposed safeguards include holding limits and no interest.

sources.limits: Euro-area example only. Do not describe intended capabilities as deployed, hypothetical holding-limit scenarios as chosen limits, or proposed regulation as adopted law.
sources.access: Official FAQ read; update date visible.

sources.title: Project Polaris: handbook for offline payments with CBDC

claims.text: Offline CBDC design joins technology choices to privacy, inclusion, risk and operating responsibilities.
Device replacement, purse reprovisioning and offline-value recovery require explicit treatment rather than assuming an online backup solves them.

sources.limits: No universal offline solution; evidence from researched designs is not assurance of tamper resistance or safe unrestricted offline recirculation.
sources.access: Official publication page and PDF relevant sections read.

sources.status: Published framework and control objectives; not a certification

claims.text: Security is an ecosystem lifecycle spanning preparation, identification, protection, detection, response, recovery and adaptation.
claims.support_location: Sections 5–6; Appendix A Recover and Adapt; Appendix B

claims.text: Recovery should preserve transaction status and participant positions; cryptographic migration and cross-organisation responsibilities require planning.

sources.title: Options for access to and interoperability of CBDCs for cross-border payments
sources.publisher: CPMI, BIS Innovation Hub, IMF and World Bank
sources.status: Published joint analytical report to the G20

claims.text: Interoperability models include compatible standards, interlinked systems and a common system.
Foreign access, legal arrangements, governance and coordination matter alongside technology; no model is universally appropriate.

sources.limits: Interoperability is not established merely by deploying on a shared chain or exposing an API. FX and participant access need separate decisions.
sources.access: Official publication page and PDF relevant sections read.

sources.title: Recommendation for Key Management: Part 1 – General, SP 800-57 Part 1 Revision 5
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.status: Final Revision 5 as served; Revision 6 initial public draft also listed

claims.text: Key management includes lifecycle protection, inventory, compromise response, replacement and recovery planning.
Split-knowledge handling prevents any single individual from acquiring all key shares under the stated procedures.

sources.limits: General technical guidance, not CBDC law. Recheck current algorithm guidance and revisions before implementation; do not infer that every key should be backed up.
sources.access: Official final page and PDF relevant sections read; project page checked.
